I've saved the Q3 answers to `/work/answer.json`. Running the same logic on Q2 first reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| 항목 | 값 |
|---|---|
| a. 순매출 1위 세그먼트 | consumer, 308,453,332원 |
| b. 결제 완료 고객 수 | 248명 |
| c. 순매출 1위 카테고리 | acc, 301,822,291원 |
| d. 순매출 최대 월 | 2025-09 |
| e. 환불액 합계 1위 고객 | u32@ex.com |
| f. 결제 완료 주문 2건 이상 고객 | 238명 |
| g. 주문당 평균 순매출 | 685,248원 |
| h. 8월 대비 9월 증가율 | 0.7% |

The database has data-quality issues that affect these numbers. I tried every combination of the plausible readings below, and only one matched all the Q2 values. Every other combination got at least one value wrong:

- **Time zone:** Order times are stored in UTC (`...Z`). I converted them to Korean time (UTC+9) before assigning months and quarters. Using UTC as stored gets most of the Q2 values wrong.
- **Segment labels:** The same segment is written different ways, such as `Enterprise ` (trailing space) and `enterprise`, or `SMB` and `smb`. I trimmed spaces and lowercased them. Each order's segment comes from the customer record that placed the order.
- **Duplicate customers:** The `customers` table has 300 rows but only 250 distinct emails, so 45 emails appear on more than one record. For b, e and f I counted each email as one customer. Counting record IDs instead gets b and f wrong for Q2.
